filed: 2026-11-10, before run.py ran; never edited after the run (a dated report instead)
seen_before_filing: experiments/update_svd/results/spread.json: the effective rank of the 16 rank-1 and cipher states at step 10 (the card's spread), so the rank-1 vs cipher pair's reading was seen before filing: side means about 427.6 and 429.2, ranges 8.7 and 11.4

definitions.erank: primary. Per matrix, exp(H(p)) with p = s / sum(s), s the singular values of dW (Roy and Vetterli 2007); per state the ||dW_m||^2-weighted mean over the 24 decomposed matrices, as E51 (experiments/baseline_weights/run.py, Base.matrix and Base.state). Undefined (null) at dW = 0
definitions.top10: secondary, not scored: share of ||dW||^2 in the 10 largest singular values of dW, same weighting
definitions.norm2: secondary, not scored: ||dW||^2 summed over the 24 matrices
definitions.r: the re-gating share of each saved state, copied from experiments/method_table/results/scorecard.json (method r) for exactly the states read here
definitions.pair rule: for a reading X on a pair: gap = mean of X over the side built to reuse minus mean over the side built to be new; range = the larger of the two sides' max - min; ratio = gap / range; separates iff |gap| > range, strict (E51's rule, experiments/baseline_weights/results/predictions.json). Sign reported, not used by the rule
definitions.covered pairs: every scorecard pair with a saved dW for at least two states per side, listed in run.py PAIRS; holes are listed in results.json

edge_cases_checked_before_filing.zero update: erank and top10 null, norm2 0; never enters a pair. Expected and checked in the control
edge_cases_checked_before_filing.one state on a side: range would be 0 and any gap would separate: a pair with fewer than two states on a side is not covered (none of the covered pairs has fewer than two); the code asserts it
edge_cases_checked_before_filing.ties: |gap| == range does not separate; all states equal (gap 0, range 0) does not separate; ratio 0/0 is reported as 0
edge_cases_checked_before_filing.range 0, gap not 0: separates; ratio reported as +-inf and drawn at the axis end
edge_cases_checked_before_filing.sign: a negative gap (reuse side lower) separates as a positive one does; the sign is reported per pair and in P3

control.order: runs first and alone; any miss stops the job before any saved state is read (exit 1)
control.rank10: per matrix of the 24 shapes, 10 orthonormal pairs with equal singular values: erank within 1e-6 of 10, top10 within 1e-9 of 1
control.rank1: the same with one pair: erank within 1e-9 of 1, top10 within 1e-9 of 1
control.zero: dW = 0 on every matrix: erank null, top10 null, norm2 0
control.e51_reproduction: ident32_s0 and rand32_s0 (regating_table) read erank within 1e-6 (relative) of E51's results.json states.<name>.agg.erank, 442.4947 and 427.5242

P1.claim: the card's split: the effective rank separates at least as many covered pairs as the share does (rival A), against fewer (rival B)
P1.rule: count_erank = covered pairs where erank separates; count_r = the same for r on the same states. Rival A iff count_erank >= count_r; rival B iff count_erank < count_r
P1.why: E51's separation by the rank was at the edge of the rule (24.5 against 23.9) and followed the update's size; the rank-1 vs cipher pair, seen before filing, does not separate

P2.claim: the effective rank separates at least one covered pair the share does not
P2.rule: true iff some covered pair has erank separating and r not separating
P2.why: the share does not separate the two label pairs, whose sides were trained for different numbers of steps (case label 30 against 300, repeat label 30 against 100), and the rank followed size in E51

P3.claim: on every covered pair the effective rank separates, the side built to reuse has the higher rank
P3.rule: true iff sign(gap) > 0 on every pair where erank separates; vacuous (reported as 'none separate') if count_erank = 0
P3.why: E51's copy side read higher, but the rank followed size and size does not run one way across the built pairs

reported_not_scored: top10 and norm2 by the same pair rule
